fonts.why: Redundant with Plus Jakarta Sans pick; no italic limits accent flexibility.

fonts.name: Plus Jakarta Sans

fonts.name: Outfit
fonts.why: Redundant geometric sans, thinner strokes fade over blurred/light backgrounds at body sizes.

fonts.name: DM Sans
fonts.why: Strong alternate body pick but redundant once Inter is chosen; kept out to avoid two near-identical humanist sans.

fonts.name: Sora

fonts.name: Urbanist

fonts.name: Lexend

fonts.name: Figtree

fonts.name: Syne

fonts.name: Unbounded

fonts.name: Albert Sans

fonts.name: Be Vietnam Pro

fonts.name: Red Hat Display

fonts.name: Hanken Grotesk
fonts.why: Not on candidate list; verified as a viable alt-body (see notes) but not selected over Inter for this school.

fonts.name: Sofia Sans
fonts.why: Not on candidate list; verified as a viable alt-heading (see notes) but not selected.

fonts.name: Schibsted Grotesk

notes: All 19 candidate lookups done via npm view (both @fontsource/ and @fontsource-variable/ scopes) and api.fontsource.org/v1/fonts/<slug>; both sources reachable, no fallback needed. Poppins and Be Vietnam Pro exist only as static packages (E404 on -variable scope), confirmed by fontsource API variable:false. All 19 candidates have latin in their subsets. No mono face fits glassmorphism's signature (frosted panels/UI, not code); omitted rather than forced. Space Grotesk chosen for accent instead of heading specifically to keep clear of Vaporwave's likely retro-tech heading signature. Three off-list faces verified the same way (npm view + fontsource API), all exist/latin/variable: Hanken Grotesk (viable Inter alternative for body, slightly more character in the grotesk terminals), Sofia Sans (viable Plus Jakarta Sans alternative for heading, extremely wide weight range 100-900 with italics, very soft geometric feel matching frosted UI), Schibsted Grotesk (viable Space Grotesk alternative for accent, has italics which Space Grotesk lacks, useful for emphasis chips on glass cards).

notes:
All npm lookups done live 09-13-26; "" recorded for every @fontsource-variable/* that returned npm E404 (confirmed one log: real 404, not a transient error). Fontsource API (api.fontsource.org/v1/fonts/<slug>) reachable for all 23 candidates; latin=true for every one (defSubset:"latin" and "latin" present in subsets array in each response). Variable axes not exposed directly in the /v1/fonts payload (no "axes" key in the JSON); axes listed above (wght, plus opsz for Bodoni Moda) are from known Google Fonts variable-axis registrations for these families, not the API response itself - flag if the pipeline needs axis data to be API-verified rather than general-knowledge-verified.

Non-candidate faces that would suit grandmillennial better than several list entries, verified via the same two lookups:
1. Cormorant Upright (Cormorant sub-family with an upright-italic-like decorative cut) - does NOT exist as its own @fontsource slug; Cormorant covers it via style, so no separate faces gained. Skip.
2. Fraunces (@fontsource/fraunces + @fontsource-variable/fraunces, both exist, latin=true, variable axes wght/opsz/SOFT/WONK) - a wet-ink old-style serif with dramatic optical-size swing that reads even more "ornate historical printed page" than Cormorant Garamond at display sizes; strong alternate heading or body-display pairing partner.
3. Petit Formal Script (@fontsource/petit-formal-script exists, no variable package, latin=true, weight 400) - an actual formal copperplate/calligraphy-class script (Google Fonts "handwriting" formal subtype), arguably a tighter fit for "formal script accent" than the more casual scripts on the list; worth a side-by-side against Pinyon Script.
4. Cormorant Infant is not a separate slug (folded into Cormorant), so not counted as a third alternate; instead: Italiana's sibling "Prata" already covered - no third addition needed beyond Fraunces and Petit Formal Script above.

Safe picks all verified exists=true, latin=true; heading and body both use a variable package (Playfair Display, Cormorant Garamond). Accent (Pinyon Script) has no variable package because none is published for it - static-only is correct here.

notes:
Mono pick: @fontsource/ibm-plex-mono (static only, weights 100-700, latin=true, italic=true) for labels/specs/captions — technical and neutral, keeps grid annotations legible without borrowing a dev-tool mono's connotation.

Three off-list candidates verified the same way (npm view + api.fontsource.org), all latin=true, all with @fontsource-variable packages at 5.3.0:
1. Roboto Flex — @fontsource-variable/roboto-flex, styles=[normal] only (no italic), a genuinely neutral engineered grotesk built for wide axis control (width/weight/optical size/slant registered in Google's own axis reg, though this API instance only reports the base font, not full axis list); best alternate heading if Archivo's proportions feel too American/geometric and something closer to Helvetica's tighter apertures is wanted.
2. Barlow — @fontsource/barlow only (no variable package on npm), weights 100-900 + italic, latin=true; a condensed-adjacent grotesk descended from California highway signage, gives Swiss-style tight tracking and a genuine 9-weight range for a strict type scale.
3. Overpass — @fontsource-variable/overpass, weights 100-900 + italic, latin=true; also highway-gothic derived (Interstate-class), slightly more geometric than Barlow, solid alternate body/heading pairing partner if Public Sans feels too civic/American-government in tone.

All npm lookups used `npm view @fontsource[-variable]/<slug> version`; a 404 (E404) was confirmed by inspecting the full npm error output, not just tail -1, for ibm-plex-mono, space-mono, instrument-serif, and atkinson-hyperlegible variable packages (none exist). Fontsource metadata came from https://api.fontsource.org/v1/fonts/<slug> (subsets/weights/styles) plus https://api.fontsource.org/v1/variable/<slug> (axis keys) since the /fonts endpoint's `variable` field is a boolean, not an axis object.

Didn't touch any repo files; read-only survey per instructions.

fonts.why: NOT ON CANDIDATE LIST: tall geometric condensed caps with genuine 1930s poster-lettering lineage, strong alternate/co-heading pick to Poiret One when a bolder single-weight display is needed

notes: All 37 candidates exist on npm and report latin=true via the Fontsource API; no rejects were for existence/latin, only stylistic fit or cross-school collision. Heading: Poiret One is the canonical Poiret/geometric high-waisted deco display (single 400 weight, so pair sparingly with a heavier companion like Bebas Neue for contrast). Body: Cinzel (variable package, weights 400-900) chosen over Bodoni Moda/Playfair Display SC/Libre Bodoni to avoid three overlapping Didones — Cinzel's engraved-capitals character is more distinctly deco than a generic high-contrast serif, and it has full latin + variable weight support for real typographic range. Accent: Miltonian is the strongest shaded/engraved accent found (with Miltonian Tattoo and Fascinate Inline as backups; Cinzel Decorative also viable for ornamental swash headlines). Rejected Marcellus deliberately — it is already this codebase's signature AR-card/showcase face (docs/ar-card/HANDOFF.md, #73), so reusing it here would blur brand identity across schools. Rejected Josefin Sans, Oswald, and Big Shoulders Display as reserved workhorse sans faces likely claimed by Bauhaus/Swiss-class schools elsewhere in the survey; rejected Bungee Shade and Monoton as belonging to a Vaporwave/neon school instead. Three faces NOT on the candidate list verified via the same two lookups (npm + Fontsource API, all latin=true, all @fontsource-only, no variable package): (1) Bebas Neue — tall geometric condensed caps, genuine 1930s American poster-lettering pedigree, a strong second heading option; (2) Spectral SC — small-caps serif with an engraved quality, a possible body alternate; (3) Alegreya SC — small-caps humanist serif, weaker deco signal than Spectral SC but latin-verified as a fallback. Caveat: Fontsource API 'variable' field returns an empty array (not axis names) for every family here that does have a variable package (Cinzel, Bodoni Moda, Oswald, etc.) — the presence of a resolvable @fontsource-variable/* npm package was used as the source of truth for variable_package/exists rather than the API's variable field, and axis names are not exposed by this endpoint (recorded as empty arrays throughout).

notes:
All 31 candidates resolved on npm and the Fontsource API; every one carries a 'latin' subset. npm view: base @fontsource/<slug> exists for all 31 (v5.3.0); @fontsource-variable/<slug> exists only for playfair-display, cormorant-garamond, bodoni-moda, orbitron, exo-2, noto-sans-jp, noto-serif-jp, inter — every other slug 404s on the variable package (confirmed via explicit E404 grep), meaning those ship static-only.

Role logic: heading = classical serif set bold/italic or display caps (Bodoni Moda safe-pick; Playfair Display, Libre Caslon Display as alts). body = Exo 2, the only techno-flavored sans in the set that stays legible at running-text sizes with italic + variable weight (Rajdhani as condensed alt, no italic/variable). mono = VT323 safe-pick (Press Start 2P/Share Tech Mono/Space Mono as alts by legibility trade-off). accent = split across wide-techno-display (Orbitron, Audiowide, Michroma, Syncopate, Monoton, Righteous, Bungee family, Zen Dots, Iceland, Wallpoet, Major Mono Display) and Japanese katakana faces (Dela Gothic One safe-pick for bold display use; Noto Sans/Serif JP, M PLUS 1p, Sawarabi Mincho, Zen Tokyo Zoo as alts depending on whether the use is decorative headline vs. legible running Japanese text).

Rejected: Comic Neue (wrong tonal register — casual/handwriting, not Y2K chrome) and Inter (too neutral/contemporary; reserved this generic grotesk register for a school like Glassmorphism so Vaporwave doesn't collide on a plain-UI heading/body face).

Cross-school constraint: heading pick (Bodoni Moda, ornate high-contrast Didone italic) is deliberately far from what a Glassmorphism school would use (expected to be a soft neutral geometric sans like Inter/Manrope/Poppins), so no heading collision expected — flagging as an assumption since Glassmorphism's own picks weren't surveyed in this run.

Three off-list faces verified the same way (npm + Fontsource API), all latin=true, static-only (no @fontsource-variable package — confirmed E404):
- Chakra Petch (@fontsource/chakra-petch, weights 300-700, has italic) — angular Thai-designed techno sans, reads closer to actual sci-fi HUD type than Orbitron/Audiowide; strong heading/accent alt.
- Turret Road (@fontsource/turret-road, weights 200-800) — chunky techno-slab display with real weight range, good for a heavier accent than Zen Dots/Iceland.
- Trispace (@fontsource/trispace, weights 100-800, variable package DOES exist @fontsource-variable/trispace) — techno monospace-flavored sans with a working variable axis, a better body/UI candidate than Rajdhani since it has both latin coverage and variable weight and reads terminal-adjacent without the eye-strain of a true mono like VT323/Share Tech Mono.
